clue.text: Sailors' constant anticipation about a dance

indicators.note: 'about' places one thing around another, so the expectation wraps the sailors and the constant

blocks.note: hope is looking forward to something
RN is the Royal Navy, the usual crossword sailors
pi is the mathematical constant

explanation.surface: Sailors are eagerly looking forward to a dance on shore.
explanation.walkthrough: The navy and the constant sit side by side, wrapped by the expectation word.
explanation.definitionFit: The hornpipe is a lively solo jig traditionally associated with seamen aboard ship.

clue.text: Fall out, perhaps, in the north

definitions.note: dialect adverb, 'in the north' tells us where

blocks.note: first meaning: to occur or come about
second meaning: in northern English dialect, the word means maybe

explanation.surface: Perhaps people up north are having a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall out' looks like a quarrel but means to come to pass. In Yorkshire and Lancashire speech the word is used for 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that fall out simply take place, and northern English dialect uses the same word for maybe.

clue.text: In time he'll ensure a personal appointment for you

definitions.text: In time he'll ensure a personal appointment for you

indicators.note: 'In' tells us the word sits inside the run of letters that follows, across the word breaks

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the middle word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: An assistant promises that you will eventually get a private meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines the answer: the Grim Reaper, Death personified, keeps an appointment with everyone in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grim Reaper personifies death, whose one meeting with each mortal is inevitable.

clue.text: Display a grim hairstyle?  Hardly

blocks.note: pomp is splendid display
taken as written
dour means stern and grim
surface padding: an ironic comment that the showy style is anything but grim

explanation.surface: Is a grim hairstyle something to show off? Hardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardly' comments that this showy swept-up style is the opposite of grim.
explanation.definitionFit: The pompadour is a style with hair swept up high from the forehead, named after Madame de Pompadour.

clue.text: Drama featuring soldier Elvis played

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are performed in a new arrangement

blocks.note: a private is a soldier of the lowest rank
taken as written

explanation.surface: A play in which a soldier character called Elvis appears.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel Coward's 1930 comedy of divorced couples is a well-known stage play.

clue.text: There's point in moral principle applied to race

indicators.note: 'in' sets the compass point inside the larger word that follows

blocks.note: an ethic is a moral principle
N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A moral argument is being brought to bear on questions of race.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes something relating to a people's racial or cultural origin, as in ethnic groups.

clue.text: Characteristic of rat, or not

indicators.note: 'or not' says the two letters o and r are to be left out

blocks.note: a rat is a betrayer

explanation.surface: Is this typical of a rodent or not?
explanation.walkthrough: TRAITOR without OR leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait is a distinguishing quality or feature of someone's personality.

clue.text: Last drink of the day with a bird

blocks.note: the last part of the day is night
a jar is a drink, and 'of the day' completes the picture of night as the day's last part

explanation.surface: A final evening tipple taken while watching birds.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'last of the day' plus 'drink': a jar is British slang for a drink, often of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The nightjar is a nocturnal insect-eating bird with a churring call.

clue.text: Office worker held in ongoing disrespect

indicators.note: something held in is enclosed, so this word sits inside the next

blocks.note: cont. is the abbreviation for continuing
a temp is a temporary office worker

explanation.surface: A temporary office worker is treated with constant disrespect.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt is scorn, the feeling that someone is beneath consideration.

clue.text: Fruit of the sea?

blocks.note: a pear is a fruit
the main is a poetic word for the open ocean

explanation.surface: It looks like a riddle about seafood, the fruit of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit' does double duty: it is the definition and also supplies the first part.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearmain is an old variety of apple, so it is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Gas from leading jurist?

indicators.note: 'leading' asks for just the front letter of the word it describes

blocks.note: the first letter of jurist
argon is an inert gas

explanation.surface: A top lawyer is talking hot air.
explanation.walkthrough: The gas comes after the leading letter. Read as a whole, the clue also describes the answer: the technical 'gas' a lawyer spouts.
explanation.definitionFit: Jargon is impenetrable specialist language, the kind of empty talk or 'gas' a lawyer can produce.

clue.text: Transport unfortunately isn't arriving ...

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone awry, so the letters land in the wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A grumble that the trains are late again.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that this rail company was famous for late running. Virgin Trains ran intercity services in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgin Trains was a British rail operator, so it was a company providing transport.

clue.text: Backwash?

blocks.note: surface reading: the water pushed back by a wave or a boat
setter's reading: a wash for the backside, a medical flushing of the bowel

explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' is a euphemism for the rear end here, so a 'back wash' is a rectal cleansing.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical procedure injects fluid into the rectum to flush out the lower bowel.

clue.text: His philosophy was composed of toil and tears

definitions.text: His philosophy was composed of toil and tears

indicators.note: something composed is put together anew, so the following letters are arranged into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gloomy thinker whose whole outlook was hard work and sorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, wittily, while its last words supply the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek thinker, pupil of Plato, is among the most famous philosophers in history.

clue.text: Timbre?

blocks.note: surface reading: the tone quality of a voice or instrument
setter's reading: the French word for a postage label

explanation.walkthrough: In French, timbre means a postage stamp, so the word itself names something from abroad that goes on a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Timbre is the French term for the adhesive postal label, hence a postage item from another country.

clue.text: ... dependent on being temporarily unavailable

blocks.note: first meaning: hanging down from something
second meaning: put on hold for a while

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the late trains are reliant on being withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to the clue before. 'Dependent' here is the literal sense, hanging from.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hanging from a hook is literally dependent, and a service halted for now is put on hold.

clue.text: Voice raised in row on the river

blocks.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
a set-to is a quarrel or row

explanation.surface: Someone shouts during a rowing race on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the river first in a down answer. 'Row' looks like rowing but is a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is the artificially high register a male singer uses above his normal range.

clue.text: To college fellows, leisurely progress means disorderly haste

blocks.note: the SCR, senior common room, is where college fellows meet
to amble is to walk at a relaxed pace

explanation.surface: Academics think a slow stroll counts as a frantic rush.
explanation.walkthrough: SCR is the Senior Common Room at Oxford and Cambridge colleges.
explanation.definitionFit: A scramble is a hurried, chaotic rush, such as a scramble for seats.

clue.text: One's instrumental in making peace with Israeli supporter though not at frist

indicators.note: 'not at first' tells us to drop the opening letter of the supporter word ('frist' is a slip for 'first')

blocks.note: an accord is a peace agreement
a Zionist supports the state of Israel

explanation.surface: Someone plays a key role in brokering a peace deal involving Israel's backers.
explanation.walkthrough: ZIONIST loses its Z to give IONIST. 'One's instrumental' is a pun: the person plays an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plays the squeezebox is literally an instrumental performer, punning on being instrumental in something.

clue.text: Snack for a prophet in South Africa

indicators.note: 'in' puts the prophet inside the country abbreviation

blocks.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa
Amos is an Old Testament prophet

explanation.surface: Food is laid on for a visiting prophet in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A samosa is a fried triangular pastry with a spiced filling, a popular light bite.

clue.text: Rank, pretentious rubbish is held in some suspicion

indicators.note: something held in is enclosed, so the rubbish goes inside the other word

blocks.note: sus is a slang shortening of suspicion, only part of the word
tat is tawdry, showy junk

explanation.surface: Showy, pretentious junk is regarded with some suspicion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like an adjective for foul-smelling, but it is a noun meaning standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is one's standing or position in a social or professional hierarchy.

clue.text: Gill is of little account

blocks.note: first meaning, cryptically: a gill is a small measure, so a small amount of ale
second meaning: something trivial or unimportant

explanation.surface: Someone called Gill is being dismissed as unimportant.
explanation.walkthrough: Gill looks like a woman's name, but it is a quarter-pint measure. The phrase is an idiom for something trifling.
explanation.definitionFit: A gill is a modest measure of ale, while the idiom describes trivial matters not worth bothering about.

clue.text: Willingly give a pound to the old woman

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling
a, meaning one, is the Roman numeral I
Eve is the first, and so the oldest, woman

explanation.surface: Someone is happy to hand a pound to an elderly lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieve is an archaic form of lief, meaning gladly or readily, as in 'I had as lief'.

clue.text: Screw that's not begun to screw?

indicators.note: something not begun is missing its start, so the opening letter goes

blocks.note: a screw, in slang, is an act of intercourse

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about one twisting fastener turning another.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Screw' is the vulgar noun: SEX ACT, which loses its S. The second is the verb meaning to extort.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact money is to extract it by force or pressure, the slang sense of squeezing someone.

clue.text: What the doctor ordered for getting fit to enter the race

indicators.note: something that enters goes inside, so this word is placed within the other

blocks.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
fit to do something is able to do it

explanation.surface: A doctor prescribes something to get a runner fit to compete.
explanation.definitionFit: A pill is the classic item a physician prescribes, so this is exactly what is prescribed.

clue.text: Troubled mind in a mob taken by the devil

indicators.note: something troubled is stirred up and disturbed, so the following letters are jumbled
'in' places the jumbled letters inside the crowd word

blocks.note: a host is a great crowd
taken as written

explanation.surface: An anxious person is lost in a crowd seized by the devil.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes from the proverb 'devil take the hindmost', the one at the back gets caught.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says the devil seizes whoever lags last, so the rearmost person is the one carried off.

clue.text: 'ouse rented, of course

blocks.note: a house is a home, and the apostrophe drops the H as a Cockney would
a property that is let is rented out

explanation.surface: A Cockney remark that of course the house is rented.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H in 'ouse signals dropping the H from the synonym too.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg dish served at a meal is one course among the dishes making it up.

clue.text: Old vehicles scared us silly

indicators.note: silly means senseless, so the letters before it are knocked out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Rickety old cars have frightened us badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand automobiles sold on by previous owners are not new, so they are old motors.
